newsitem.title: FRANCE: France fires state firm boss in privatization row.
newsitem.headline: France fires state firm boss in privatization row.

text.p: The French government fired GAN state insurance firm Chairman Jean-Jacques Bonnaud Wednesday following a fall-out over a scrapped bank privatisation and named Didier Pfeiffer from rival insurer UAP to replace him.
Government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said a decree removing Bonnaud had been approved at a cabinet meeting.
UAP said in a statement Finance Minister Jean Arthuis had named UAP Vice-President Pfeiffer as successor at Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN).

The rare firing of a state-appointed chairman by decree followed a government decision in mid-November to scrap a tender for the privatisation of GAN bank subsidiary CIC and charges by Arthuis that Bonnaud and CIC Chairman Bernard Yoncourt failed to promote the sell-off.
Lamassoure declined to comment on the removal of Bonnaud, who argued that heeding a government call to resign amounted to an admission of guilt and he believed he had done no wrong.
Pfeiffer, who has served a string of successive chairmen in over 24 years at UAP, will not be replaced as vice-president.
